title: Sources of Change on an Enrollment in the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
A retiree joins a plan of the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans because their sponsor names them on its eligibility file, and the plan confirms their Medicare entitlement before coverage begins.

## The condition on a change being recorded

The change being recorded comes from the sponsor's eligibility file or a written sponsor instruction where it is a roster or contribution change, and from the retiree themselves where it is a disenrollment.

The source of a change is read from the plan's own change records before the change is recorded or the enrollment amended, and it is read on the change record itself. The three sources the records may carry are the sponsor's eligibility file, a written sponsor instruction, and the retiree's own request.

### The same rule as a question of authority

A retiree may never add themselves to a group, and a sponsor may never disenroll a retiree who has not asked to leave: each change has exactly one proper source, and a change from the wrong source is refused and its source told why.

## How far back a roster change may reach

A sponsor may add a retiree back as far as the tier's retroactive addition months and remove one as far as its retroactive removal months; anything further back is handled as a reconciliation rather than as a roster change.

## The lag the plan allows

The plan allows the tier's file lag between a change happening at the sponsor and its appearing on the file, and a retiree calling inside that lag is told the change may not yet be visible rather than that it has not happened.

## What every change record holds

Every change records what the record said before and what it says now, so that a retiree disputing a contribution can be shown exactly when it changed and on whose instruction.

A retiree who says their employer told them something different is taken seriously and the sponsor is asked, but the plan never changes a record on the retiree's account of what the sponsor said.
